findings.title: Immediate email cancellation has no retry or DB state change
findings.body: In the immediateDelete branch, the function posts a SendGrid cancellation but returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder or setting cancelled. If that request fails, the catch only logs and leaves the row unchanged. On reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts:968) this leaves the old reminder with cancelled null, so scheduleEmailReminders will never retry it and the old SendGrid email can still be delivered. On workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx:214, 521) the related row may then be cascade-deleted, making retry impossible even though the SendGrid cancellation failed. Mark the row cancelled before the API call or delete it only after a successful cancel, and provide a retry path on failure.

findings.title: A single SendGrid cancellation failure prevents deleting already-cancelled reminder rows
findings.body: The loop awaits one SendGrid cancel request at a time and only awaits the collected prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises after the loop. If any client.request throws, control jumps to catch, so the DB deletes for previous successfully cancelled reminders never execute. Those rows remain cancelled: true and will be retried on the next cron run, causing duplicate SendGrid cancellation requests for the same batch IDs and potentially keeping stale rows longer. Move each row delete immediately after its successful SendGrid call or use Promise.allSettled/individual try-catch so one failure doesn't block cleanup of other reminders.

findings.title: No tests cover deferred/immediate cancellation behavior
findings.body: This PR changes the cancellation flow to a deferred cron-based cancel for normal cancellations and an immediate branch for reschedule/deletion, but no tests were added for how rows are updated/deleted when referenceId is null, when immediateDelete succeeds or fails, or how scheduleEmailReminders picks up cancelled rows. Given this fixes a production notification bug, regression tests for these paths would prevent the same failure mode.
